clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2. At each of the 30 runtime calls the gcc streams make: argument registers, what is saved before the call, whether vector registers survive it, stack alignment, and whether the result pointer may alias an argument.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read the package disassembly in the unit's work directory. Emitter::mul stores 0 in the spill_avx byte at 0x38395e, while udiv at 0x383a9e and mulmod at 0x38760e store 1, as the item says. monad_vm_runtime_mul (out/fn/000000000044e160.s) uses only rax, rcx, rdx and r8 to r13, pushes r12 and r13, and has no vector instruction, so keeping ymm words live across it is safe. It loads all four limbs of the rdx operand and limb 0 of the rsi operand before its first store to [rdi] at 0x44e19b, never reads rsi limb 0 again, and stores limbs 1 to 3 only after its last read at 0x44e1de. A result pointer equal to either argument therefore gives the right product.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3. The runtime helpers run from the package text in the x86 model, 48,000 standalone and 27,000 aliased cases with 0 mismatches.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I transcribed monad_vm_runtime_mul 0x44e160 to 0x44e1f6 instruction by instruction, with the carry chain of each add and adc as listed, into my own Python model in the scratchpad. It gave the product mod 2^256 on a 17 by 17 grid of edge words (0 to 3, 2^64 and its neighbour, 2^128, 2^192, 2^255, 2^256 - 1, 2^96, 2^160, 1e6, MIN_SQRT_PRICE, MAX_SQRT_PRICE) and on 200,000 random operand pairs of 64 to 256 bits, with no mismatch. I did not re-run udiv, umod or mulmod myself and rely on the unit's helpers.json for them.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 6. No block writes a word that differs between the gcc build, the clang harness and pyevm.py, so an ordinary account gains nothing and locks nothing through these blocks; the validator still runs Monad/0.16.7 and the PoolManager code is unchanged.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The chain facts hold. I queried https://rpc.monad.xyz on 2026-11-27: web3_clientVersion returned Monad/0.16.7, eth_blockNumber returned 0x78035c6, and eth_getCode of 0x188d586ddcf52439676ca21a244753fa19f9ea8e at latest returned 24,009 bytes with sha256 288b97729c9e4f346195d6d31cf7d1edf5eb13b352d538b338b2df0d85a7b0d3, equal to networks.json and the unit's rpc.log. The words claim holds for the value-computing sites. The conclusion that nothing is gained or locked goes further than the evidence. The unit's own Task 4 and coverage.json say the 128 terminators of these blocks have not run from the package, and those include the JUMPI with a deferred comparison that decides require(denominator > prod1) at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:30, the prod1 == 0 branch at :33 and the rounding branch at :112. A wrong branch there would change a swap amount or a revert without changing any word the unit compared. The item is correct for words and unproven for branch decisions. I found no fault in it, so I add a medium-priority lead and not a high one.
